from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Circles of all sizes share a secret ratio.", "Small hamster wheels, large Ferris wheels alike.", "This special ratio is always the same."]
        self.setup_layout("The Hook: The Constant Ratio", lecture_lines)
        
        # Load Assets
        hamster = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/hamster.svg")
        wheel = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/wheel.svg")
        
        circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color="#FFFFFF")
        circle_group = VGroup(circle, hamster)
        self.place_in_area(circle_group, 'B3', 'E5', scale_factor=0.75)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(circle_group), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Represent diameter and radius
        radius_line = Line(circle.get_center(), circle.get_right(), color="#FF0000")
        radius_label = Text("r", font_size=20, color="#FF0000").next_to(radius_line, UP)
        diameter_line = Line(circle.get_left(), circle.get_right(), color="#00FF00")
        diameter_label = Text("d", font_size=20, color="#00FF00").next_to(diameter_line, DOWN)
        
        self.play(Create(radius_line), Write(radius_label), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.play(Create(diameter_line), Write(diameter_label))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        d_eq_2r = MathTex("d = 2r", color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(d_eq_2r, 'E4', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.place_at_grid(wheel, 'A3', scale_factor=0.5)
        
        self.play(Write(d_eq_2r), FadeIn(wheel), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Defining Pi (π)", [
            "Pi is circumference divided by diameter.",
            "Unwind the string around the circle.",
            "It takes three lengths plus a remainder."
        ])
        
        # Assets
        circle_img = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/circle.svg")
        string_img = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/string.svg")
        
        # Elements (Adjusted per criticism)
        circle = self.place_at_grid(circle_img, "C4", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        diameter = Line(circle.get_left(), circle.get_right(), color="#00FF00")
        label_d = Text("d", font_size=24, color="#00FF00").next_to(diameter, DOWN)
        
        circumference = Arc(radius=circle.width/2, start_angle=0, angle=2*PI, color="#FFFF00")
        label_c = Text("C", font_size=24, color="#FFFF00").next_to(circle, UP)
        
        ratio_label = self.place_at_grid(Text("C / d = π", font_size=32, color="#FF6600"), "D4", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        remainder_string = self.place_in_area(string_img, 'E3', 'E5', scale_factor=0.7)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(circle))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Create(circumference), Write(label_c))
        self.play(Create(diameter), Write(label_d))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(Write(ratio_label))
        self.play(FadeIn(remainder_string))
        self.play(Indicate(ratio_label), run_time=2)
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF6600"))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Ancient cultures estimated Pi differently.", "Archimedes used polygons to trap circles.", "More sides mean a better estimate."]
        self.setup_layout("Historical Evolution: From Estimation to Precision", lecture_lines)
        
        circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(circle, 'C5', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show Egyptian/Babylonian approximations
        approx_text = VGroup(
            Text("Babylonians: π ≈ 3", font_size=24, color="#CCCCCC"),
            Text("Egyptians: π ≈ 3.16", font_size=24, color="#CCCCCC")
        ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        self.place_at_grid(approx_text, 'E5', scale_factor=0.7)
        
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(approx_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Archimedes' polygon method
        polygon = RegularPolygon(n=4, radius=1.6, color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(polygon, 'C5', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(polygon))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Increase sides
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        for n in [6, 8, 12, 24, 64]:
            new_polygon = RegularPolygon(n=n, radius=1.6, color=BLUE)
            self.place_at_grid(new_polygon, 'C5', scale_factor=0.6)
            self.play(Transform(polygon, new_polygon), run_time=0.5)
            
        modern_pi = Text("Modern π ≈ 3.14159", font_size=28, color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(modern_pi, 'E6', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(Write(modern_pi))
        self.wait(2)

        self.setup_layout("The Irrational Nature of Pi", ["Pi is an irrational number.", "It never ends and never repeats.", "Computers can never find its end."])
        
        # Animation Elements

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Pi bridges linear and curved geometry.", "Vital for GPS and space travel.", "Pi keeps our world connected."]
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Real-World Relevance", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        arch = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/arch.svg", color=BLUE)
        engineering = VGroup(arch)
        
        sat_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/satellite.svg", color=YELLOW)
        orbit = Circle(radius=0.8, color=RED)
        orbit_eq = MathTex(r"C = 2\pi r", color=WHITE)
        space = VGroup(sat_icon, orbit, orbit_eq).arrange(DOWN)
        
        pi_sym = MathTex(r"\pi", color=GREEN).scale(3)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.place_at_grid(engineering, 'B4', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(engineering))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.place_at_grid(space, 'C5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(space))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.place_at_grid(pi_sym, 'E4', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Flash(pi_sym.get_center(), color=GREEN))
        self.play(FadeIn(pi_sym))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Mystery of Pi: Definition and History

sections.title: The Hook: The Constant Ratio
sections.content: Introduce the concept that no matter the size of a circle, the ratio of its circumference to its diameter is always the same. Use a visual of a rolling bicycle wheel versus a giant Ferris wheel to show they share this 'secret' number.
sections.example: If a hamster runs in a wheel with a 10cm diameter, its path length is exactly 10π cm.

sections.title: Defining Pi (π)
sections.content: Formal definition: π = C / d (Circumference divided by Diameter). Use an animation where a string is unwound from a circle's circumference and laid against the diameter line to show it takes exactly 3 lengths plus a small remainder (the 0.14...) to cover the distance.
sections.example: Visualizing a pizza: slicing it into infinite thin triangles to show how the circumference relates to the radius.

sections.title: Historical Evolution: From Estimation to Precision
sections.content: Briefly trace history: The Ancient Babylonians used 3, the Egyptians estimated 3.16, and Archimedes used 'polygons' to trap the circle (inscribed/circumscribed). Visualize Archimedes adding more and more sides to a polygon until it 'becomes' a circle.
sections.example: Comparing a square (4 sides) inside a circle vs. a 100-sided polygon inside a circle to show how the shape gets 'closer' to the truth.

sections.title: The Irrational Nature of Pi
sections.content: Explain that π is an irrational number—it never ends and never repeats. This implies that no matter how much computing power we use, we can never reach the 'end' of Pi.
sections.example: A robot trying to memorize Pi and running out of memory capacity because the digits go on forever.

sections.title: Summary and Real-World Relevance
sections.content: Reiterate: Pi is the fundamental bridge between linear measurements and curved geometry. It is used today in GPS systems, space travel, and quantum physics.
sections.example: A satellite navigation system calculating the orbit of a planet around a sun using π to ensure it doesn't crash.
